fragments.text: Back in 2020, around the time when UNESCO's recommendation on the ethics of artificial intelligence was being drafted, we started to come together in the Caribbean really to understand where we were with artificial intelligence. And so the Caribbean AI initiative was started. The UNESCO Caribbean Artificial Intelligence AI Policy Roadmap was developed under the Caribbean The Caribbean AI Initiative, two extensive consultation with experts, policy makers and community leaders. The desire to have broader consultation with Caribbean stakeholders resulted in consultations with over a thousand institutions and individuals, including women and youth, in over 20 countries in the region. In addition, there were eight different regional consultations as well regarding the actual pillars themselves. The Caribbean AI Initiative was started to better understand the region's readiness in

regards to the global standard UNESCO recommendation on the ethics of AI. Well the Caribbean AI Initiative began, the kernel really was the thinking of the Broadcasting Commission that we couldn't have exponential technologies, frontier technologies, changing all the operating systems of the society, and we sit by and observe. The commission took the initiative to engage with the UNESCO information for all program and the Caribbean cluster office for UNESCO and the subject. I'm thinking about artificial intelligence and engaging around artificial intelligence from the ground up, not the other way around. So this new Caribbean AI policy roadmap is really necessary and I would say essential

for addressing the unique challenges but also the great opportunities that artificial intelligence presents to seeds, to small island development states. Artificial intelligence development is a global endeavor and I'm happy that the development of this roadmap was undertaken with extensive regional and international collaboration and is a timely input to help carry come since. The roadmap can guide the development of AI technologies that boost productivity, innovation and competitiveness in various sectors. The roadmap advocates for comprehensive national and regional AI strategies, ethical guidelines and collaboration with international partners to ensure that AI development is inclusive, sustainable and human-centered. So we're acknowledging that the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence places a tremendous opportunity ahead of us here in the Caribbean but also many risks.

And so, to address this, the UNESCO AI Policy Roadmap offers a policy framework for development and regional collaboration, and it's really built on four pillars, culture and creativity, governance and transformation, education and upskilling and resiliency and sustainability. So this roadmap really serves as a blueprint for member states to navigate these challenges by setting ethical guidelines, by setting the needs of capacity building, first of all, identify the needs and build up on it to foster collaboration between international, national and local stakeholders. With this roadmap, we can guide governments, industries, academia, institutions in implementing AI solutions that is tailored for our own regional problems that these would include healthcare, culture and arts and data protection and privacy. And so I

think that the roadmap emphasizes the need for regulatory frameworks, regional regulatory frameworks, that manage the ethical concerns and ensure that AI I developed in a way that is aligned with the region needs. And the roadmap recommends tools like the ethical impact assessment from UNESCO to ensure transparency and accountability in AI systems. For privacy and security, we know that there is a rapid increase in the use of biometric systems, such as facial recognition and fingerprint recognition. and we've really lacked strong governance in the region. So the roadmap stresses the need for laws that protect personal data, prioritizing policies for high risk use cases in industries such as healthcare, justice, and education. Caribbean countries must act now

to develop a multi-dimensional strategy that pushes AI governance, education, and the digital infrastructure across the region while preserving human creativity, increasing trust and protecting the environment to enable the region's transformation and the survival in the digital age. Our call of action is really the governments, you know, academia, private sector, civil society at all levels, including indigenous people and community, must unite to develop a comprehensive artificial intelligence strategies that focus on culture, governance, education, but in particular, the resilience and the digital infrastructure. The magnitude of AI impact demands really strong leadership. It demands long-term investments and also coordinated efforts across all sectors. So together we must ensure that artificial intelligence benefits everyone in the Caribbean that is inclusive while mitigating risks.
